_note: Core/Integrity (F17.4) — the platform-neutral corpus for server-verifiable app attestation. The capability is NOT device posture (Mandatory/Security answers that, and an attacker simply lies to it): it is a token the developer's BACKEND verifies with Apple or Google, so the trust anchor is off-device. What is pinned here is therefore the REQUEST validation and the ENVELOPE SHAPE, so one server can be written against one contract instead of sniffing which mobile OS sent the request. There is deliberately no client-side verdict to pin. Read by kernel/test/integrity-conformance.test.ts (TS, reference), :core IntegrityConformanceTest (Kotlin) and Engine/iOS/Integrity.swift.

limits._note: 500 is Play Integrity's nonce ceiling and is the BINDING constraint across both platforms: Apple hashes the challenge so any length works there. One rule, so a challenge that works on one platform cannot fail on the other.
